title: Onity Compatible RFID Hotel Key Cards — Legacy to Modern Migration Matrix
summary: ProudTek RFID cards are fully compatible with Onity (Honeywell) hotel locks across the Trillium RFID flagship, HT RFID series, and legacy HT24 magstripe-only models using MIFARE Classic, MIFARE Plus, MIFARE Ultralight and MIFARE Ultralight C chips via ISO/IEC 14443A. Many of the world's largest hotel chains operate Onity lock ecosystems that are still transitioning from magstripe-only HT24 systems to RFID-capable HT RFID or modern Trillium locks. This magstripe-to-RFID migration path is not a simple switch — properties must navigate chip compatibility, PMS encoding integration, and simultaneous magstripe and RFID issuance during transition periods. The compatibility matrix on this page maps every Onity lock series to its supported chip families, DirectKey mobile access capability, encoding platform and the exact ProudTek card SKU verified through internal test-bench encoding using both legacy HT RFID and modern Trillium reference hardware. Properties can execute a phased RFID migration by specifying dual-interface cards with both magnetic stripe and RFID in parallel chipsets. Request a free Onity test-card kit covering legacy magstripe, pure RFID and hybrid dual-interface credentials to validate your specific lock models and encoding workflow before bulk production.

sections.intro: Onity properties span three generations of lock technology — legacy HT24 magstripe, transitional HT RFID dual-interface and modern Trillium RFID. Choosing the right chip family depends on your current lock generation and migration timeline.

callout.label: Migration rule
callout.text: Properties transitioning from HT24 magstripe to Trillium RFID should order dual-interface cards (magstripe + RFID) during the transition phase. Once all locks are upgraded to Trillium and guests have been re-issued RFID-only cards, the magstripe component becomes optional and can be discontinued to reduce per-card cost.

sections.title: Why Chip and Interface Selection Matters for Onity Properties
sections.intro: Onity lock suites present a unique challenge — many properties operate a mix of legacy HT24 magstripe, transitional HT RFID, and modern Trillium locks simultaneously. The wrong chip or interface choice can fragment your access control and complicate guest issuance.

before: All credentials encoded via magstripe (ISO 7811) — no RFID capability
Guest card reader hardware limited to magstripe stripe readers at front desk and locks
No mobile access options or PMS middleware integration — direct encoder-to-lock flow
Card replacement requires hardware magstripe stripe writing — slower encoding cycles
Legacy HT24 locks remain operational indefinitely but cannot upgrade to RFID without hardware swap
after: All credentials encoded via OnPortal PMS integration with MIFARE RFID chips
Guest card reader hardware modern — contactless RFID readers faster and more reliable than magstripe swipe
Mobile access optional — Trillium DirectKey BLE module enables smartphone NFC unlock alongside physical cards
Fast encoding — RFID cards programmed in under 2 seconds vs 5-8 seconds for magstripe writer
Future-proof — Trillium supports next-generation chip families and cloud-based access control

sections.title: Onity Magstripe-to-RFID Migration Workflow
sections.intro: Properties executing a staged RFID migration from legacy HT24 magstripe locks must follow a phased approach to maintain guest access during the lock hardware upgrade cycle.

items.label: Phase 1 — Baseline magstripe operations
items.text: Property operates all HT24 locks with ISO 7811 magstripe credentials. ProudTek provides plain magstripe cards or branded magstripe + RFID dual-interface cards in preparation for next phase.

items.label: Phase 2 — HT RFID lock deployment
items.text: Property begins replacing HT24 magstripe locks with HT RFID dual-interface capable locks (supports both magstripe and RFID). New locks accept magstripe cards from Phase 1 plus new RFID cards for staff testing.

items.label: Phase 3 — Dual-credential issuance period
items.text: All guest rooms have either HT24 magstripe or HT RFID dual-interface locks. ProudTek ships dual-interface RFID + magstripe combo cards. Guests with HT24 locks get magstripe; guests with HT RFID locks get combo cards.

items.label: Phase 4 — Trillium RFID full rollout
items.text: All HT24 and HT RFID locks decommissioned and replaced with Trillium RFID modern locks. OnPortal takes over encoding. ProudTek ships pure RFID cards (no magstripe) — cost savings with no legacy payload.

items.label: Phase 5 — Optional mobile access (DirectKey)
items.text: Property activates Trillium DirectKey BLE module. Guests with NFC-capable phones can unlock via mobile app. ProudTek provides mobile credential sync support; physical RFID cards remain as backup.

faq.question: What chip works with all current Onity lock generations?
faq.answer: MIFARE Classic is supported on all HT RFID legacy locks. MIFARE Ultralight C is the universal standard across HT RFID and Trillium. MIFARE Plus is preferred for Trillium modern locks and supports enhanced AES mutual-authentication. For properties mixing HT RFID and Trillium in the same estate, MIFARE Ultralight C is the safest universal chip choice.

faq.question: Can I use a single card to unlock both HT24 magstripe and Trillium RFID locks?
faq.answer: Yes, with dual-interface combo cards. ProudTek manufactures cards with both ISO 7811 magstripe AND RFID MIFARE chip on a single physical card body. This is the standard approach during Phase 2-3 of a magstripe-to-RFID migration when both lock types are operational in the same property.

faq.question: What is DirectKey, and do I need it for Onity compatibility?
faq.answer: DirectKey is an optional BLE (Bluetooth Low Energy) module on Trillium locks that enables smartphone NFC unlock alongside physical RFID cards. It is not required for basic Onity compatibility. Properties can operate Trillium locks with pure RFID cards and no mobile access. DirectKey is a future enhancement available during Phase 5 of a modern RFID deployment.

faq.question: How do I know if my property is on HT24, HT RFID or Trillium locks?
faq.answer: Check the physical lock label — it will say HT24 (magstripe only), HT RFID (dual-interface capable) or Trillium (modern RFID). If unsure, take a current guest card sample to ProudTek — we can identify the lock type from the card. HT24 cards are always magstripe-only; HT RFID and Trillium cards are RFID-based.

faq.question: Can ProudTek pre-encode Onity-compatible cards?
faq.answer: ProudTek ships cards with correct chip and magstripe encoding configuration but does not pre-encode guest-room RFID credentials, as room keys require real-time PMS data from OnPortal including room number, check-in date and access level. Guest rooms must be encoded at your property. However, ProudTek can pre-encode common-area service keys if the property provides access-group definitions.

faq.question: What is the minimum order quantity for Onity-compatible cards?
faq.answer: RFID-only cards start at 200 pieces for plain white stock. Dual-interface magstripe + RFID combos start at 300 pieces due to dual-encode setup cost. Test-card kits including magstripe-only, RFID-only and combo variants are available at no charge for new migration projects. Volume pricing tiers begin at 5,000 and 10,000 pieces with cost reductions of 12-18%.

faq.question: How long does an Onity compatibility verification and migration planning take?
faq.answer: A baseline compatibility check takes 3-5 business days. If you are executing a phased migration from HT24 to Trillium, the full planning and testing cycle takes 12-18 business days. Test-kit shipment and on-site validation takes 3 days plus 5-7 days for migration timeline analysis and artwork approval. Rush services available for properties on accelerated lock replacement schedules.

faq.question: What happens if I order RFID-only cards when my property still has HT24 magstripe locks?
faq.answer: HT24 magstripe-only locks will not read RFID cards — they require magstripe stripe input. Guest lockouts will occur at check-in. The solution is to either order dual-interface combo cards during the transition, or delay RFID-only card orders until all HT24 locks have been replaced with HT RFID or Trillium. Always verify your complete lock inventory before ordering.

faq.question: Does Onity support MIFARE DESFire chips?
faq.answer: Legacy HT RFID does not support MIFARE DESFire. Modern Trillium RFID locks with firmware version 3.5 or later support MIFARE DESFire EV2. If your Trillium firmware is earlier than 3.5, stick with MIFARE Plus or MIFARE Ultralight C. Check your Trillium firmware version in OnPortal settings before specifying DESFire for compatibility.
